newsitem.title: USA: Mississippi prepared to try tobacco suit.
newsitem.headline: Mississippi prepared to try tobacco suit.

text.p: Mississippi is prepared to go ahead with a trial of its suit against the tobacco industry on July 7 unless a settlement is reached, Mississippi Attorney General Mike Moore said Tuesday.
"They have two options, the industry, at this point. They either settle my case or we try," Moore told reporters at a meeting of state attorneys general in Wyoming.
Any settlement of the Mississippi case would be separate from the proposed nationwide settlement with the tobacco industry announced by state attorneys general last Friday.
Mississippi was the first of 40 states to sue the tobacco industry to recoup medical costs of treating ill smokers. It sued in May 1994.
The proposed $368.5 billion national settlement is designed to end the 40 state lawsuits, but it needs congressional action, which could take months.

Moore, who led the national talks, said he planned to hold talks with tobacco industry representatives on the Mississippi case later this week. He would not say where the talks would be held and would give no hint of what he would seek in a possible settlement. The trial is scheduled to start July 7.
"I'm going to go negotiate with the industry about Mississippi now. I didn't feel comfortable doing that until this negotiation was done because I was leading the negotiations," he said.
"But because my trial date comes up, I can't afford to move my trial date. I think it would do a disservice to the people I represent. I don't want to be behind all those big states," Moore said.

Moore acknowledged that there was a risk that the whole agreement could fall apart if he went to trial. "So I've got a lot of leverage on my side at this very moment, don't I? And I've got to use it for the benefit of both country and my state. So that's what I'm trying to do," he said.

Florida Attorney General Bob Butterworth said earlier Tuesday that his state was pushing ahead with preparations for a trial of its suit against the tobacco industry. He denied a published report the state was negotiating with the industry to delay the trial, scheduled to start Aug. 4.

"We're not going to delay our trial, no way...I spoke to my governor last night and I'm meeting him tomorrow and we're talking about trial strategy. We're ready to go to trial," Butterworth told Reuters.
